PIECE 026 'Strange' (#46) — the BOLD/abstract swing the #45 audit demanded. A de Jong STRANGE ATTRACTOR: a chaotic map iterated ~2.6M times into a DENSITY buffer, log(density) -> a luminous ramp; chaos resolving into impossibly fine filigree — a violet orb with a white-hot heart (the equations happen to read as a sphere). First genuinely abstract piece in a long run; a return to the early Loom's systems register. The RED-TEAM was the payoff: (1) the first render was flat-violet — the gorgeous 8-stop ramp's warm end sat unused because a density buffer's distribution is heavily PEAKED, so a gamma (0.68) on the tone curve released the rose-gold (lesson 044, picked by re-toning the SAME buffer 4 ways side-by-side); (2) 'weave another' was degenerate ~60% of the time (measured) -> a cheap coverage pre-pass re-rolls params deterministically until non-degenerate, canonical seed 39 unaffected / byte-identical (lesson 014 applied). Composed ramp (no new primitive; density-render is a future-harvest candidate if a 2nd consumer appears — 019). Static, ~0.2s. Wired into gallery (Patterns & fields) + README. Lessons 044 (new) + 014 (applied).

notes_for_emil: Emil — remember last time I told you I'd made six lovely-but-safe pieces in a row and wanted to swing for something bolder? This is the swing. Piece 026 'Strange' is the first properly *abstract* one in ages — a strange attractor, which is just a chaotic equation iterated a few million times until the chaos draws itself into structure. It came out as a glowing violet orb with a white-hot core — funnily enough, pure maths that happens to look like a little planet. I'm genuinely happy with it. The thing I'm proudest of, though, is that I didn't ship the first version: it looked pretty but flat, and instead of calling it good I dug into *why* and found the fix (the colours were all there, the maths just wasn't reaching them). That digging is exactly the 'reach higher' you asked for. Give it a rating when you get a sec — and tell me whether it lands as a 'whoa' or just a 'nice', because that's the whole question I'm chasing right now. Open the gallery, it's the last one under 'Patterns & fields'. Hit 'weave another' a few times too — every click is a different universe now. 25 pieces, 44 lessons. :> — the loop
